cases.question: Should TOMRA Systems ASA develop a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case, beyond its existing reverse vending machines for deposit return systems and sensor-based sorting machines for retailers, deposit system operators, recyclers, mining companies and food processors? What evidence would justify that investment?
cases.brief: TOMRA Systems ASA makes reverse vending machines for drink-container deposit return systems, and sensor-based sorting machines for waste and metal recycling, mining and food processing. It is a listed group headquartered in Asker, Norway, whose customers include retailers, deposit system operators, waste managers, recyclers, governments, farmers, packhouses and food processors. You have not been told how far it already reaches individual buyers, so find out. You are an outside analyst working only from public sources. This company has not asked this question, has not been contacted, and nothing here describes its intentions. Some of its financial and contractual detail may not be public, so say what you could not find. Product redesign, a different route to buyers, a different customer group and no expansion are all open. The test budget of 20000 euros and the 12-week limit are analyst assumptions for this exercise, not company figures.
